items.title: Il Fatto Quotidiano: Milan Fashion Week Sept 22-28 calendar published as Italian fashion sector loses revenue and exports
items.summary: Italian daily's Milan Fashion Week SS27 guide confirms 203 appointments (61 shows including Prada opening Sept 22, Armani closing Sept 27) and flags Gucci's Friday slot as one of three closely watched 'second collections' (with Fendi's Chiuri, Marni's Rogge). Frames the whole week against a fragile Italian fashion sector reporting falling turnover and exports -- explicit critical/macro framing rather than pure show promotion.

items.title: MilanoFinanza: full Milan Fashion Week September 2026 event calendar confirms Gucci's Friday show
items.summary: Italian financial-trade outlet lists the complete SS27 Milan Fashion Week calendar (Sept 22-28), confirming Gucci shows Friday Sept 25 at 2pm as Demna's second in-person runway collection for the house, alongside Prada's first-ever September opening slot. Service/business journalism, neutral tone, positions Gucci as a bellwether appointment investors and press are watching.

items.title: ad-hoc-news.de: Kering stock steady on Euronext as investors await confirmation of Gucci-led recovery
items.summary: German financial outlet reports Kering shares trading broadly flat on Euronext Paris ahead of Milan Fashion Week, with analysts and investors watching whether Gucci's improved H1 2026 US retail momentum converts into sustained positive comparable sales rather than a still-negative print. Neutral financial-market read, not brand-authored; flags that current share price may already discount recovery hopes.

items.title: BFM Bourse: Kering shares jump 11% as Gucci nears return to growth, but analysts still want proof
items.summary: French financial-markets outlet covers Kering's H1 2026 results: Gucci's comparable sales decline narrowed to 2% in Q2 (vs. -8% in Q1), driven partly by North America; Kering stock jumped on the print but analysts remained cautious, wanting sustained quarters of evidence before calling the turnaround real. Included for financial-market context corroborating the Sept 13 steady-stock read; flagged as older than ideal freshness window but load-bearing for interpreting this week's stock commentary.

items.title: nss magazine: Is Gucci really lowering its prices under Luca de Meo
items.summary: Italian trade outlet documents quiet summer 2026 price cuts across Gucci product lines under CEO Luca de Meo -- sneakers down from EUR800 to EUR560-595, polo from EUR650 to EUR455, T-shirt from EUR550 to EUR385, Jackie Slim medium now under EUR2,000. De Meo quoted acknowledging the group had 'pushed prices a little too high' and that prior increases are 'no longer feasible today.' Critical-angle business story implicitly conceding past overpricing; still actively cited in trade commentary this month.

items.title: PurseForum thread: buyer flags uneven stitching on a new GG Marmont mini, sparks quality-control debate
items.summary: Community thread (distinct from an earlier quality-concerns thread) where a buyer describes visibly uneven corner stitching on a newly purchased GG Marmont mini shoulder bag; store staff showed alternate units but the original was judged the best of the batch. Replies split -- several members say recent Gucci quality is 'pretty good' in their experience, others share their own stitching/alignment checklists, some compare unfavorably to Louis Vuitton, Fendi and Hermes. Genuine unmoderated consumer quality-control chatter; engagement counts (replies/views) not exposed in the fetched view, left null.

items.title: Instagram: Gucci official account recap post of Fall/Winter 2026 collection ahead of second Milan show
items.summary: Gucci's own Instagram account posts a highlights recap of the Fall/Winter 2026 collection in the run-up to Demna's second in-person Milan show (Sept 25). Brand-owned activation content, discounted per sentiment-rubric treatment of owned-channel marketing; included for buzz/volume tracking only. Public like/comment counts were not retrievable via the fetched view, left null.

items.title: Coveteur essay: 'Are We Asking Too Much of Today's Designers?' revisits the Demna-Gucci controversy
items.summary: Independent culture-and-fashion outlet essay argues critics and social media may be placing unrealistic turnaround expectations on Demna at Gucci, reviewing the FW26 debut's mixed reception and asking whether commercial pressure has made audiences unable to judge a collection on creative terms alone. Critical-but-sympathetic community-adjacent commentary; dated March 2026 so outside the ideal freshness window but kept as the most substantive available discourse-style item surfaced this run on the 'is criticism of Demna fair' angle -- flagged as stale by policy, weight should reflect this.

items.title: BoF: Demna's Gucci back under the microscope as Milan Fashion Week opens
items.summary: Trade press previews Demna's second in-person Gucci runway show (Sept 25, Milan) as a test of whether February's reset is producing lasting cultural and commercial traction a year into his tenure. Notes the show lands the same week as Fendi's Chiuri and Marni's Rogge second collections, positioning Gucci as a bellwether for the 2027 bag conversation. Balanced anticipatory framing that raises open questions rather than assuming success.
